label: dense near-always-on feature (every step except t=0); strongest around copying m
explanation: Dense feature: active on 85.5% of all steps and in every sequence. It is never active at t=0, active on 65% of t=1 steps, and on about 92-98% of every later step, in all phases, for all tokens and lengths. The rate rises somewhat as the end of the sequence nears (to_go 8: 46%, to_go 0: 97%), and the copy phase (96%) is a little above the original phase (76%). The binary predicate t >= 1 gets F1 0.96 with mass recall 1.0, but that only says the feature is on everywhere except the first step; it is not a selective explanation. Magnitude: the largest activations all come in the copy phase when the token being output, or the next one, is m. out_tok==m and next_out==m are 100% active with above-baseline mass share, but this clause covers only 14% of the top activation quartile, so the m effect is one modulator of magnitude and not a description of the feature. No other per-step or history variable (token identity, in_count, n_digits, first_tok, prev2_tok) changes the rate by more than about 1.1x.
